page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 48 physical cores with 48 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz with a dedicated allocation model and no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with 2850 GB of NVMe SSD instance store capacity, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core tests. However, single-core performance is more modest, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average and weak categories respectively. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks show average throughput, though the Passmark memory score is weak. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, show weak performance, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core metrics reach average tiers. Large-scale LLM inference tasks show poor to weak performance, particularly in text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture and dedicated physical cores offer a resource-dense profile for multi-threaded workloads without hyperthreading overhead. The inclusion of high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage makes this server suitable for workloads requiring fast local scratch space or caching. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose applications that can leverage parallel processing across its 48 dedicated cores.
